technical_accuracy_of_explore_claim: VERIFIED_ACCURATE (DS005_BYE 16-donor null +0.274d, p_2s=0.2568, q=0.4657 and Stage 3 futility confirmed)

evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Phase 3 Stage 3 RCT NCT00349622 (Cudkowicz et al. 2014 Lancet Neurol PMID:25297012, N=514 randomized [341 vs 173] / N=513 analyzed [340 at 4 g/d IV + ursodiol vs 173 placebo]) was stopped early by DSMB for futility on co-primary ALSFRS-R slope (+0.09 u/mo, -1.22 vs -1.31, p=0.2370) and survival (HR=0.90 [0.71-1.15], p=0.4146) while causing hepatobiliary AEs in 211/340 (62%) vs 19/173 (11%) (p<0.0001) and biliary SAEs in 41/340 (12.1%) vs 0/173 (0%); CHEMBL161 HTS records human EAAT2 EC50 >10 uM, Bye 2025 survival was null (+0.274d, p=0.2568, q=0.4657), and analyzed human M1 astrocyte (p=0.9086) and NYGC spinal SLC1A2 mRNA cohorts (p=0.61-0.72) show no statistically detected transcriptional reduction.

evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Bulk spinal RNA and living-CSF C1q/C4B shifts largely reflect glial proportion, center offset, or multi-copy RCCX C4B short-read CNV mapping artifacts (C4B DIA p=0.0568, q=0.3369; ~2-3% healthy European C4B*Q0 homozygosity refutes apparent LOEUF=0.257/0.413); systemic C1q ablation carries >90% SLE/encapsulated-sepsis liability — in HD Phase 2 NCT04514367 (N=28, PMC13307253, PMID:41787606), IV ANX005 (75-100 mg/kg) saturated baseline CSF C1q with downstream CSF complement reduction at 0.2-0.25% CSF:serum penetration while recording 3/28 (10.7%) treatment-related AE withdrawals and 2/28 (7.1%) drug-related SAEs (abstract: lupus + idiopathic autoimmune hemolytic anemia; Results/Table 2: SLE + non-infectious pneumonitis; hypothesized to reflect peripheral ~180 nM serum C1q sink depletion [MODEL_PRIOR]; whereas in completed open-label ALS Phase 2a NCT04569435 [17 actual participants in CT.gov registry], Annexon's 2024 Form 10-K reported 13 treated for 12 weeks, 7 of whom continued to 24 weeks, with C1q target engagement and downstream complement reduction in blood plus an exploratory sponsor-reported subgroup observation of less ALSFRS-R decline and blood NfL stabilization without peer-reviewed publication; note Annexon also advanced local intravitreal humanized anti-C1q Fab ANX007 / vonaprument into Phase 3 ARCHER II NCT06510816 — meaning only intrathecal half-life/ECM tethering is unbuilt rather than the anti-gC1q Fab warhead — and oral small-molecule C1s inhibitor ANX1502 NCT05521269 targets enzymatic C1s rather than C1q CLR-stalk RNP uptake); IV BBB-TfR-shuttled IgG is likewise modeled to deplete 99.99% of a hypothesized 180 nM serum C1q sink [MODEL_PRIOR] while unmodified q4w IT 48 kDa Fab clears via ~4x/day CSF turnover; and global C1qa KO failed to extend SOD1 mouse survival while worsening cholinergic C-bouton loss (Lobsiger et al. 2013 PMID:24170856; cf. aging CNS C1q accumulation Stephan et al. 2013 PMID:23946404).
factual_justification: Per Epistemic Asymmetry, systemic C3 failure in MERIDIAN (C024, unmeasured CSF PK / limited intact-BBB entry expected) did not test CNS parenchymal C1q or C3-independent neuronal C1q RNP biology (Scott-Hewitt et al. 2024, 10.1016/j.cell.2024.05.058), whereas RCCX comparator C4B is confounded/null. Completed open-label ALS Phase 2a NCT04569435 enrolled 17 actual participants (sponsor 2024 10-K reports 13 treated for 12 weeks, 7 continuing to 24 weeks, with blood C1q target engagement/downstream complement reduction and an exploratory sponsor-reported subgroup observation of less ALSFRS-R decline and blood NfL stabilization), whereas CSF C1q saturation was reported in HD NCT04514367 (PMID:41787606) alongside 3/28 AE withdrawals & 2/28 drug-related SAEs (peripheral ~180 nM serum C1q sink hypothesized [MODEL_PRIOR]; IV TfR-IgG serum depletion 99.99% [MODEL_PRIOR]) and unmodified q4w IT Fab washes out (t1/2 ~12 h), retaining C018 in Tier 3 for half-life-extended intrathecal C1q blockade gated on spinal C-bouton preservation.
discriminating_next_test: Engineer ECM-anchored half-life-extended intrathecal anti-C1q Fab/nanobody or intrathecal microglial C1QA/B 2'-O-MOE ASO/di-siRNA (rejecting systemic IV ANX005, IV BBB-shuttled IgG, and unmodified q4w IT 48 kDa Fab) and gate on preserved cholinergic C-bouton (SLC18A3/SLC5A7) and neuronal RNP proteostasis in adult spinal cord models (PMID:24170856; 10.1016/j.cell.2024.05.058).

name: Baricitinib
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Rank #2/107 in Bye 2025 pure sALS iPSC-MNs (+3.774d, 14/16 lines, p=2.56e-7, q=6.85e-6); TDP-43 KD induces neuronal JAK2 3'UTR shortening (dPAS=-0.4391, padj=2.96e-61) & AAK1 lengthening (dPAS=+0.1673, padj=6.32e-16) replicated by Edinburgh excitatory JAK2 upregulation (+0.4907, p=0.0457, n=34); NYGC ALS-Glia enriches gp130/OSMR->JAK1/2->STAT3 (cortex z_diff=+0.7031, p=6.27e-4, AUC=0.7893; cord z_diff=+0.4169, p=1.91e-6, AUC=0.7186, whereas NYGC cord Type-I IFN/TYK2 is flat p=0.843); originating C9orf72 dsRNA JAK-STAT rationale (Rodriguez, Albers et al. 2021 PMID:34233951) motivated 24-wk open-label NADALS (NCT05189106, conducted 2022-2025, N=9 ALS enrolled, 5/9 completers; 2->4 mg QD; n=8 PK), showing 1.748 nM Wk8 & 3.804 nM Wk16 2h post-dose total CSF entry (<4 nM unbound vs proposed 50 nM target ceiling; <7% modeled TYK2 occupancy) with descriptive pre/post -38.1% CSF CXCL10 change and stable CSF NfL (uncontrolled pre/post CXCL10 does not establish direct CNS JAK occupancy), while subsequent cortical TDP-43 cdsRNA->TYK2 experiments (Konig et al. 2026 PMID:41832177) quantified untreated G298S iPSC-N K1 dsRNA IF + ReNcell VM poly(I:C) baricitinib EC50=135.9 nM (35.7x above 3.804 nM total ALS CSF), ruxolitinib EC50=152 nM vs ~1.5-4 nM Cu,CSF, & BBB-excluded deucravacitinib EC50=1.48-16.21 nM (cf. brain-penetrant JAK2-sparing dual TYK2/JAK1 JH1 inhibitor BHV-8000 / TLL-041 in early PD NCT06976268; sponsor PK disclosure Kp,uu=0.539, 20 mg QD Cu,brain,avg ~172 nM).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: P-gp/BCRP efflux limits Kp,uu,CSF to ~0.05-0.11 (3.80 nM CSF = 0.095x whole-cell pSTAT IC50 ~40 nM [~8.7% cellular occupancy]; 657x below 2.5 uM screen); NADALS ALS had 1/9 PE SAE + 1/9 DVT event (1-2/9 [11.1-22.2%] ALS participants; un-deduplicated in NCT05189106 aggregate AE table; 2 AEs rated Possibly Related, 0 Probably/Definitely Related; 4/9 non-completers); structural/mechanistic JAK1-vs-neuronal-JAK2 catch-22 where JAK2-sparing selective JAK1 JH1 inhibitors forfeit TDP-43-induced autonomous neuronal JAK2 survival rescue (if 2.5 uM Bye rescue requires neuronal JAK2 or saturating AAK1/kinome polypharmacology) whereas retaining JAK2 hits EPO/TPO and JAK1/2 VTE walls; allosteric TYK2-JH2 spares gp130/OSMR->JAK1/2->STAT3 (cord TypeI-IFN/TYK2 axis p=0.843, AUC=0.508) and neuronal JAK2; shotgun MS CSF CXCL10 suffers left-censored MNAR/tryptic scarcity (31.3% DIA / 84.2% TMT missing), is Emory-matched center-null (symp_als p=0.838, sALS p=0.602), and is orthogonal (DIA r=+0.0517, TMT r=-0.366) to the 4-protein high-chitinase CSF glial panel; gnomAD v4.1 MANE JAK1 LOEUF=0.168, JAK2 LOEUF=0.848 (Open Targets 0.178/0.739) + FDA Boxed Warnings bar unstratified chronic dosing.
factual_justification: Descriptive open-label ALS CSF CXCL10 pre/post change (-38.1% at 4 mg/d, N=9 uncontrolled) and neuronal TDP-43 JAK2 3'UTR APA + pure-MN survival rescue alongside gp130/OSMR->JAK1/2->STAT3 ALS-Glia enrichment forbid DROP under Epistemic Asymmetry, but C019 is recalibrated to the Tier 3 exploratory watchlist because 3.80 nM CSF (~8.7% modeled cellular pSTAT occupancy; 35.7x below Konig 2026 ReNcell EC50=135.9 nM and 657x below the 2.5 uM screen), NADALS recorded 1/9 PE SAE + 1/9 DVT event across N=9 ALS participants (un-deduplicated in aggregate registry), case-vs-control CHIT1-adjusted CSF AUCs do not establish Baricitinib treatment prediction, and JAK2-sparing selective JAK1 inhibition creates a mechanistic catch-22 by forfeiting cell-autonomous neuronal JAK2 coverage.
discriminating_next_test: Resolve the JAK1-vs-neuronal-JAK2 catch-22 at clinically reachable unbound human CSF concentrations (3.8-50 nM; ~8.7% whole-cell pSTAT occupancy at 3.8 nM vs 39-40% cell-free JAK1/2) by testing Baricitinib vs Kp,uu-verified homodimeric-JAK2 (EPO/TPO)-sparing selective JAK1 JH1 inhibitors and CRISPRi JAK1/JAK2/AAK1 knockdowns across BOTH glia-free sALS iPSC-MNs (testing whether 2.5 uM rescue vanishes at 4-50 nM or upon JAK2 sparing) and reactive ALS-Glia co-cultures — barring co-dosing with low-dose IL-2 (EALS-031) and mandating VTE thromboprophylaxis — before any high-chitinase CSF glial-stratum-stratified (rs3831317-neutral sALS-p80) interaction trial.

name: Apilimod
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Apilimod (free base CHEMBL4297643 MW 418.49 Da; originating C9orf72 PIKFYVE iPSC-MN discovery Shi et al. 2018 Nat Med PMID:29400714 & sporadic TDP-43 validation Hung et al. 2023 Cell PMID:36754049; cf. AcuraStem/Takeda intrathecal PIKFYVE ASO AS-202) rescues mean Bye 2025 sALS iPSC-MN survival at 2.5 uM (+1.837d, 12/16 lines, p=0.00210, q=0.0173); AIT-101 dimesylate 125 mg BID (MW 610.70 Da, fu,p<0.01) in C9orf72-ALS Phase 2a (NCT05163886, N=15, Babu et al. 2024 Brain PMID:38606777) reached 283.13 ng/mL Wk12 1h plasma (n=9/10; Wk24 OG000 315.40 ng/mL, n=5) and 1.63 ng/mL (3.89 nM free-base eq) Wk12 1h CSF across 9 of 10 randomized apilimod participants (Kp,uu~0.72), cutting 12-wk randomized CSF poly(GP) by 73% in published analysis (-74.4% posted CT.gov registry) with >2.5x plasma sGPNMB target-engagement rise (Babu Table 3 shared-baseline repeated-measures mixed-model plasma ratio 2.31 [95% CI 1.56-3.41], p<0.001 vs CSF sGPNMB ratio 0.92 [90% CI 0.80-1.07], p=0.352 NS; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05163886 separately labels both analyses a 2-sided t-test), CSF NfL -5.0% (6,706.8->6,372.7 pg/mL vs +9.1% pbo), and 0 drug-related SAEs.
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Trautwig 2025 CSF GDI2 is quantified and non-significant in sALS vs Ctrl (DIA diff_log2=+0.0200, p=0.5042, n=122 within N=259; TMT +0.0245, p=0.2085; C9 only p=0.00598/0.0268); 4/16 (25%, 0 ties) sALS lines worsened at 2.5 uM; preclinical PIKfyve blockade triggers neuronal ClC-7 osmotic vacuolation and +PI(3)P->LRRK2/CASM stress (PIKFYVE gnomAD v4.1 MANE LOEUF=0.523, MGI brain vacuoles; PMID:42900584; PMID:42994990); in AIT-101 NCT05163886 (Babu et al. 2024 Brain PMID:38606777, 0 drug-related SAEs), Wk12 CSF sGPNMB showed no clear group difference (Babu Table 3 shared-baseline mixed-model ratio 0.92 [90% CI 0.80-1.07], p=0.352 vs plasma sGPNMB ratio 2.31, p<0.001; both separately labeled 2-sided t-test on CT.gov) alongside exploratory active-arm Wk12 plasma NfL median +39% (+39.2% registry, n=9) & Wk24 OLE CSF NfL mean +50% (+49.7%, n=4); and in distinct inhibitor VRG50635 studies (which cannot establish a single class-wide threshold with AIT-101), NL81735.056.22 (PMID:41708347, PMC12916242; HV NCT06286475 N=22 completed) recorded 2/6 (33%) MAD drug-related encephalopathy/renal SAEs while 400-800 mg QD ALS Ph1b NCT06215755 (54 enrolled, 50 treated; AAN2026-003396) recorded investigator-reported treatment-related SAEs in 8/50 (16.0%) treated participants plus exploratory astrocytic GFAP+NfL rises and was TERMINATED for lack of risk-benefit data supporting Phase 2 (also cautioning against months-long non-pulsable intrathecal PIKFYVE ASO AS-202).
factual_justification: 12-wk randomized C9orf72-ALS target engagement in AIT-101 NCT05163886 (-73% published / -74.4% registry CSF poly(GP), -5.0% Wk12 CSF NfL, N=15 unpowered; Babu et al. 2024 PMID:38606777) and untested sporadic ALS clinical status keep pulsed dosing open, while preclinical neuronal ClC-7 osmotic vacuolation and +PI(3)P->LRRK2/CASM stress (PMID:42900584; PMID:42994990), AIT-101 clinical observations (0 drug-related SAEs alongside exploratory small-sample Wk12 plasma NfL median +39% [n=9] and Wk24 OLE CSF NfL mean +50% [n=4]), and distinct inhibitor VRG50635 human AEs (2/6 HV MAD drug-related SAEs PMID:41708347; investigator-reported treatment-related SAEs in 8/50 [16.0%] treated participants among 54 enrolled plus exploratory NfL/GFAP rises in AAN2026-003396 / terminated NCT06215755; the two clinical programs do not establish a single class-wide toxicity threshold) motivate gating any pulsed regimen on a 14-day human iPSC-MN washout test.
discriminating_next_test: Empirically calibrate PI(3,5)P2 regeneration, ClC-7 vacuole-clearance, ATG16L1-catalyzed LC3B CASM conjugation, and LRRK2 pRab10-Thr73 washout half-lives over a strict 14-day falsification gate in C9orf72 and sALS iPSC-MNs to resolve the bifurcated q48h-q72h single-pulse nanomolar Apilimod (CHEMBL4297643) sensitivity (6.5-8.0 nM unbound Cmax passes [MODEL_PRIOR] ~79% [64/81] in decoupled dead-zone Model 1 vs ~30% [24/81] at matched 10-20h repair and 0% [0/81] at 24-48h postmitotic repair in zero-dead-zone coupled +PI(3)P->LRRK2/CASM Model 2; reconciling -PI(3,5)P2 -> ClC-7 osmotic swelling + Rab/LRRK2 hyperactivation [Clegg et al. 2026 PMID:42900584] and +PI(3)P -> direct LRRK2 + CASM amplification [Kuwahara et al. 2026 PMID:42994990, 10.26508/lsa.202603939]), co-measuring paired intracellular vs conditioned-media secreted poly(GP)/pTDP-43 mass-balance (PMID:27732842; Drosophila C9orf72 model 10.64898/2026.11.09.765393 [PREPRINT]), nanomolar-to-2.5 uM potency bridging, and fast axonal transport: advance ONLY if pulsed dosing achieves >50% net clearance with <5% ClC-7 vacuolation, tau <24 h CASM/pRab10 washout, and zero NfL/GFAP surge.

name: Icerguastat (IFB-088 / Sephin1)
causal_vs_reactive_assessment: DISPUTED_PPP1R15A_TARGET_WITH_SEVERE_PK_AND_SAFETY_LIMITATIONS: Negative reconstituted PPP1R15A-PP1c tests & disputed target interpretation, 41-71x group plasma Cmax gap under studied 25 mg BID / HV regimens, and Phase 2 fatal TEAE/fall imbalance
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Modest survival gain at 2.5 uM in Bye 2025 sALS iPSC-MNs (+1.618d, 13/16 lines, p=0.00202, q=0.0173); Zeng 2025 PPP1R15A dPAS=+0.0558 (padj=6.42e-8).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Chemical registry audit refuted misattributed IDs (verified Sephin1=CHEMBL2365743 / CID:9561611, free-base MW 196.64, acetate MW 256.69); reconstituted biochemical assays reported negative direct PPP1R15A-PP1c holophosphatase inhibition with disputed primary target interpretation (Crespillo-Casado et al. 2017/2018 PMID:28447936, PMID:29618508; while early rat motor-neuron mutant SOD1 cultures reported 10-50 nM rescue, characterized human cellular effects include 1-5 uM GluN2B NAM [Abgueguen et al. 2026 PMID:43036320] & PHB2 [Ding et al. 2026 PMID:42790826], failing SOD1-G93A mice in Vieira et al. 2024 PMID:38359044); in Phase 2 NCT05508074 (N=51 bulbar-onset ALS [88.2% sporadic], 25 mg BID + riluzole; CL/F=580 L/h in ALS, 736-1,388 L/h in HV Ph1; absolute oral bioavailability and CNS exposure ceiling unresolved), total plasma peak under the studied oral regimens was a geometric mean Cmax of 12.0 ng/mL (61.0 nM) in ALS (NCT05508074) and an arithmetic mean Cmax of 6.92 ng/mL (35.2 nM) in healthy volunteers (NCT03610334, 50 mg MAD group at Dose 2, n=6; 41-71x below 2.5 uM in total plasma; [MODEL_PRIOR] Cu,brain ~5-20 nM = 125-500x gap) with flat plasma GDF15 (~704 pg/mL posted under CT.gov ng/mL header), null ITT ALSFRS-R (-0.33, p=0.923; N=51 size limits clinical efficacy precision) & NfL ratio 1.04 (p=0.609), and 5/34 (14.7%) vs 2/17 (11.8%) total fatal TEAEs including 2/34 (5.9% vs 0%) investigator-assessed possibly drug-related sudden/cardiac fatal TEAEs and 8/34 (23.5% vs 0%) falls.
factual_justification: Excluded on low human plasma exposure under studied oral regimens, disputed primary target biochemistry, and Phase 2 safety signals: under the studied oral regimens (25 mg BID ALS CL/F=580 L/h; HV Ph1 CL/F=736-1,388 L/h; absolute oral bioavailability and a CNS exposure ceiling remain unresolved), total plasma peak was a geometric mean Cmax of 12.0 ng/mL (61.0 nM) in ALS (NCT05508074) and an arithmetic mean Cmax of 6.92 ng/mL (35.2 nM) in healthy volunteers (NCT03610334, 50 mg MAD group at Dose 2, n=6; 41-71x below nominal 2.5 uM even before protein binding; [MODEL_PRIOR] Cu,brain ~5-20 nM = 125-500x below 2.5 uM & 1-5 uM GluN2B/PHB2 activity, PMID:28447936, PMID:43036320) with flat human GDF15 and null ITT ALSFRS-R (p=0.923) / NfL (p=0.609) in bulbar-onset Phase 2 NCT05508074 (N=51, 88.2% sporadic; trial size limits standalone efficacy precision), while 25 mg BID recorded 2/34 (5.9% vs 0%) possibly drug-related sudden/cardiac fatal TEAEs (5/34 vs 2/17 all-cause) and 23.5% falls.

name: DNAJB2 (HSJ1) Cytosolic vs. ER-Prenylated Isoform Axis
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Recessive human DNAJB2 loss-of-function variants (55 Open Targets EVA/ClinVar submissions, 25/25 (100%) single-gene GRCh38 P/LP variants in shared Exons 2-9 vs 0/25 in Zone A, OMIM 614881; Chen et al. 2016 Brain PMID:26936937; dominant stop-loss c.832T>G ER-trapping neuromyopathy PMID:37070754) cause distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN5/CMT2T) and juvenile ALS, cytosolic DNAJB2a clears ubiquitylated TDP-43 aggregates in cells and rescues late-stage spinal motor neuron survival & muscle force in vivo in transgenic hHSJ1a SOD1G93A mice without extending mouse lifespan (Novoselov, Cheetham et al. 2013 PMID:24023695), and human ALS/FTD tissue shows GC-adjusted cortical oligodendrocyte mRNA (-0.745, p=3.46e-7 in BA9; -0.618, p=2.59e-4 in BA4), NYGC cervical cord mRNA (-0.293, p=5.21e-5, n=86: 48 non-mutation sALS vs 38 Ctrl), Spillman MOESM1 C9-FTD cortical homogenate DIA protein (-0.4470, p=3.05e-4, BH-FDR=0.0182, n=20; nominal synaptosome DIA trend -0.3818, p=0.00813, inconclusive after multiplicity at BH-FDR=0.2236, n=20; P25686 group does not separate DNAJB2a from DNAJB2b; PMID:42789089), and iPSC-neuron DIA protein (-1.115, p=0.0455, n=6) depletion. Primary 6-cohort splicing/APA scan confirms 0 TDP-43 cryptic/APA events (i3Neuron RNA log2FC=+0.092, p=0.124, padj=0.283), and AF-P25686-F1 resolves 2 rigid domains (aa 1-73 & 164-223, pLDDT=67.38; gnomAD v4.1 MANE ENST00000336576.10 LOEUF=0.836 vs cytosolic ENST00000392086.8 LOEUF=0.743).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Edinburgh cortical oligodendrocyte snRNA-seq is underpowered/non-significant (-0.397, p=0.447, n=33), NYGC motor cortex bulk RNA is flat (+0.087, p=0.401), CSF TMT is null (p=0.779), Spillman C9-FTD synaptosomal DIA is inconclusive after multiplicity (BH-FDR=0.2236, and P25686 peptides do not resolve DNAJB2a vs DNAJB2b), motor-neuron vs oligodendrocyte compartment dominance is unresolved, internal Intron-9 sequence (chr2:219284988-219285939(+), 952 bp sparing 5'SS 219284836-219284845, Zone A CDS/stop 219284836-219284987, and BP/PPT/3'SS 219285940-219285986 whose blockade would prevent Exon-10 splicing and force DNAJB2b!) lacks mapped ISS/intronic-polyadenylation (IPA) cis-elements, and internal Intron-9 windows sit inside the mature cytoplasmic 3'-UTR of ER-prenylated (-CVVQ) DNAJB2b mRNA where steric/shift effects risk depleting ERAD-essential DNAJB2b.
factual_justification: Anchored by human Mendelian motor-neuropathy/juvenile-ALS genetics (OMIM 614881, 25/25 single-gene GRCh38 ClinVar P/LP variants; 55 Open Targets EVA submissions), human cortical oligodendrocyte and cervical spinal cord mRNA reduction, and C9-FTD cortical homogenate DIA protein loss (-0.447, BH-FDR=0.0182; synaptosomal DIA nominal p=0.0081, inconclusive at BH-FDR=0.2236, isoform-blind P25686); retained in Tier 3 Exploratory Discovery pending sALS spinal isoform precursor quantification, Intron-9 ISS-vs-ISE mapping, and ERAD DNAJB2b safety counter-screening.
discriminating_next_test: Quantify cytosolic DNAJB2a (ENST00000392086.8, 277 aa, excising 1,151-bp Intron 9 chr2:219284836-219285986(+)) vs Intron-9-retaining ER-prenylated DNAJB2b (ENST00000336576.10, 324 aa) precursor ratios by targeted PRM/RT-ddPCR in sporadic ALS spinal cord, and benchmark intrathecal pan-CNS/oligodendrocyte-tropic AAV-DNAJB2a cDNA replacement (in vivo hHSJ1a SOD1G93A MN/force rescue without lifespan extension PMID:24023695 & cellular TDP-43 clearance PMID:26936937) against an internal Intron-9 2'-O-MOE ISS/IPA-competition microwalk restricted to chr2:219284988-219285939(+) (sparing 5'SS, Zone A CDS, and 3'SS/branchpoint chr2:219285940-219285986(+)) with mature DNAJB2b 3'-UTR stability and BiP/HSPA5 + CHOP/DDIT3 ERAD counter-screens in sALS iPSC-MN/oligodendrocyte co-cultures.

name: YKT6 (p.Tyr64Cys Longin R-SNARE)
evidence_proves_hypothesis: YKT6 (C023-N1) converges across exome-wide rare ALS risk variant p.Tyr64Cys (chr7:44206388:A>G, rs138273846 on ENST00000223369.9; Hop et al. PMID:41917433 all-ALS discovery case allele frequency=48/26,276 [0.183%; family-history-specific sALS carrier denominator unreported], OR=2.84, P=9.08e-8, meta P=1.50e-9; AlphaGenome AVI Phred=24.53, top 0.352%), direct 3.46A heavy-atom contact of Tyr64 to acyl ligand DPV201 inside Rattus norvegicus closed DPC-bound Ykt6 PDB 3KYQ (Wen et al. 2010 PMID:20159557 [Ortholog/Detergent-Analog Inferred], 4.29A from Cys66; vs human open GGTase-III [PTAR1/RABGGTB]:YKT6 PDB 6J74 PMID:32128853 establishing mandatory sequential Cys195-farnesyl -> Cys194-geranylgeranyl diprenylation required for Golgi/lysosomal trafficking, Sakata et al. 2021 PMID:33035318), TDP-43 3'UTR lengthening (dPAS=+0.1417, padj=4.57e-40), TDP-43 frameshifting 170-bp Exon-2 skip in PTAR1 (ENST00000340434.5 chr9:69750781-69750950(-), mod_3=2, MOESM11 line 4145 group E(PSI) 0.156->0.369 [MAJIQ shrunk dPSI=+0.1563], source MAJIQ 'FDR' [p_d_psi_0.05]=3.256e-6; synaptosomal PTAR1 +0.576, p=0.0158), and sALS cortical excitatory neuronal mRNA reduction (BA9 -0.464, p=4.53e-4; BA4 -0.285, p=0.0263; NYGC Motor adj beta=-0.080, p=0.035).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: YKT6 is pan-essential across 1,258 DepMap lines (mean Chronos=-1.5425, 93.8% <-1.0; gnomAD v4.1 MANE LOEUF=0.636; biallelic human YKT6 LoF disorder Ma et al. 2024 PMID:38522068) with zero known chemical ligands, p.Tyr64Cys (rs138273846; all-ALS discovery AF=0.183% [48/26,276]) has gnomAD v4.1 Joint AC=982/1,613,908 (AF=0.061%, 0 homozygotes; NFE AF=0.071% [~1:704 carriers, moderate-effect risk allele]) while the rat PDB 3KYQ Tyr64->Cys64 pocket expansion ([MODEL_PRIOR] +85.1 A^3 cavity) risks sterically ejecting endogenous Cys195-F/Cys194-GG — AND synucleinopathy/autophagy studies (Cuddy, Mazzulli et al. 2019 Neuron PMID:31648898) showed closed cytosolic YKT6 is autoinhibited and must dynamically open for SNARE assembly, warning that kinetically locking closed YKT6 (3KYQ) would block autolysosomal/Golgi fusion in non-carrier wild-type YKT6 ALS — alongside null C9-FTD synaptosomal YKT6 DIA (+0.1513, p=0.2842, n=20) and pan-essential cis-Golgi SNAREs (NSF Chronos=-2.44, DEE96; STX5 Chronos=-1.13, STX5-CDG).
factual_justification: Backed by rare human ALS coding genetics (YKT6 p.Tyr64Cys meta P=1.50e-9) and convergent TDP-43 APA + PTAR1 prenylation pathology, while extreme pan-essentiality (Chronos=-1.54) and null/toxic cis-Golgi SNARE partners (NSF, STX5, SEC22B, GOSR1, GDI2) restrict C023 to positive allele-split Longin conformational stabilization behind 4 structural and selectivity hurdles.
discriminating_next_test: Execute allele-split biophysical discovery: (1) in rare (ALS discovery AF=0.183% [48/26,276]; gnomAD NFE AF=0.071%) YKT6 p.Tyr64Cys (rs138273846) knock-in human iPSC-MNs ([MODEL_PRIOR] +85.1 A^3 Longin pocket expansion & 3.46A Cys64-Cys66 oxidation hazard in rat DPC-bound PDB 3KYQ PMID:20159557 vs human open PDB 6J74 PMID:32128853), run 19F-NMR/DSF screening for ternary [YKT6(Cys64)-prenyl + fragment] co-occupancy that prevents Cys64-Cys66 oxidation without ejecting Cys195-F/Cys194-GG OR kinetically locking YKT6 against physiological SNARE opening (k_open counter-screen on cis-Golgi STX5/GOSR1/SEC22B & autolysosomal STX17/SNAP29/VAMP8); (2) in non-carrier wild-type YKT6 ALS (family-history-specific sALS carrier denominator unreported; driven by YKT6 APA + PTAR1 170-bp Exon-2 frameshift skipping chr9:69750781-69750950(-)), test PTAR1 Exon-2 splice restoration / GGTase-III diprenylation rescue (PMID:32128853; PMID:33035318) or non-autoinhibitory exterior Longin fold chaperones preserving dynamic closed-to-open cycling (avoiding Cuddy 2019 closed-state trapping PMID:31648898).

name: Pegcetacoplan (Systemic C3 Complement — MERIDIAN)
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Focal C3 transcript elevation occurs within Zhang 2026 TDP-43+ cervical anterior-horn 55-um multicellular Visium spots (+1.2920, within-donor pseudoreplicated Seurat MAST spot bh_fdr=5.82e-23 across N=14 donors, PMID:42135512), motivating clinical testing of systemic C3 complement inhibition.
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 MERIDIAN trial (NCT04579666 posted results, N=249 started [169 vs 80] / N=247 mITT [168 pegcetacoplan 1,080 mg SC BIW vs 79 placebo]) missed Week 52 primary CAFS rank (123.0 [SE 4.71] vs 126.0 [SE 6.89]; ANCOVA LS mean diff -3.0, 95% CI -19.5 to +13.5, p=0.7205) and all secondary endpoints (ALSFRS-R p=0.6447, %SVC -6.6% p=0.0949, HHD p=0.0935, ALSAQ-40 +6.5 pts worse QoL p=0.0069) and terminated for futility, echoing systemic terminal C5 failures (Phase 3 CHAMPION-ALS ravulizumab NCT04248465 PMID:37695623; Phase 2/3 HEALEY zilucoplan NCT04436497 PMID:39960672), while living-CSF C3 fails proteome-wide FDR (DIA q=0.0708; TMT p=0.6225) and ~43.5 kDa PEGylated pegcetacoplan has unmeasured human CSF PK (limited intact-BBB entry expected against hepatic C3 synthesis, GTEx Liver=1,575 TPM).
factual_justification: Directly falsified in a 249-patient randomized placebo-controlled Phase 2 ALS trial: subcutaneous systemic C3 inhibitor pegcetacoplan (MERIDIAN NCT04579666, N=249 started / N=247 mITT [168 vs 79]: Week 52 CAFS LS mean diff -3.0, p=0.7205; ALSFRS-R p=0.6447) missed primary and all secondary endpoints alongside Phase 3 ravulizumab (NCT04248465, PMID:37695623) and Phase 2/3 HEALEY zilucoplan (NCT04436497, PMID:39960672; strictly scoped to systemic C3/C5 regimens with unmeasured/limited CNS entry, preserving CNS-compartmentalized intrathecal C1q blockade, PMID:42492371).

name: Dexmedetomidine
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Verified Bye 2025 2.5 uM paired rescue +1.3992d across 16 sALS lines (12/16 >0d, t=3.250, p=0.00538, q=0.03030, Rank #7/107).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Talke et al. 1997 paired human total plasma and lumbar CSF PK (PMID:9356115: measured ~0.20-0.35 nM total lumbar CSF = ~4% of measured total plasma; ~7,143-12,500x below the nominal 2,500 nM screen; companion CSF pressure study PMID:9249114) and FDA NDA021038 (Precedex IV ICU infusion 0.2-0.7 ug/kg/h, MW 200.28: estimated unbound plasma 0.09-0.37 nM, assuming 94% binding [fu~0.06, MODEL_PRIOR], ~6,757-27,778x below 2,500 nM; sublingual Igalmi NDA215390 23% somnolence / 18% orthostasis at estimated Cu,p ~0.18 nM) show tolerated human CNS exposure sits >7,000x below the nominal 2.5 uM screen dose (minimum effective iPSC-MN concentration unmeasured) and is gated by ADRA2A locus coeruleus unconsciousness, hypotension (25-54%), and sinus bradycardia/arrest (Ki ~1-2 nM; ADRA2A/B/C non-DE in Bye RNA-seq; oral alpha-2 agonist guanabenz had >30% ALS AE dropout in Phase 2 ProMISe, PMID:33905493).
factual_justification: Despite genuine 2.5 uM iPSC-MN rescue (+1.399d, q=0.0303; minimum effective screen concentration unmeasured), directly measured human lumbar CSF (~0.20-0.35 nM, ~4% of measured total plasma, ~7,143-12,500x below nominal 2.5 uM, Talke et al. 1997 PMID:9356115; companion CSF pressure PMID:9249114) and estimated unbound plasma 0.09-0.37 nM, assuming 94% binding [MODEL_PRIOR] (~6,757-27,778x below 2.5 uM, NDA021038), are capped by dose-limiting central alpha-2A sedation, hypotension, and bradycardia (corroborated by >30% oral alpha-2 intolerability in ALS ProMISe, PMID:33905493).

name: CuATSM
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Verified Bye 2025 2.5 uM paired rescue +1.3792d across 15 valid sALS lines (12/15 >0d, p=0.00631, q=0.03375, Rank #8/107; true ID CHEMBL4297372, fixing intake CHEMBL4297643 typo).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Randomized Phase 2/3 ALS trial NCT04082832 (72 mg/d oral, N=80 estimated, CT.gov status UNKNOWN) and completed open-label extension NCT04313166 (COMPLETED, N=55 actual) both have no posted public clinical results (hasResults=false; sponsor discontinued ALS development), observational postmortem neuropathology of treated decedents (Yang et al. 2023 PMID:37317638, PMC10947464 Table 2: N=12 brains / n=11 spinal cords mixing 5 vs 4 sporadic ALS-TDP [% TDP-43+ motor-cortex neurons 0.9% vs 5.1%, p=0.1] + 1 vs 2 ALS-SOD1) showed no significant reduction in pTDP-43 or MN loss alongside higher motor-cortex p62+ astrocyte density and fewer spinal Iba1+ microglia, [MODEL_PRIOR: 950 nM x fu 0.08 x Kp,uu 0.70 = 53.2 nM] sits ~47x below the 2.5 uM screen (bounded by 144 mg/d Phase 1 transaminitis in NCT02870634) while 62Cu/64Cu-ATSM PET (PMID:25904686) tracks hypoxic Cu(II)->Cu(I) reductive dissociation/transchelation rather than intact normoxic drug, and sporadic TDP-43 ALS lacks human genetic support for SOD1 copper chaperoning.
factual_justification: Unreported randomized Phase 2/3 outcomes in NCT04082832 (status UNKNOWN, hasResults=false) and completed OLE NCT04313166 (N=55 actual, hasResults=false) plus an underpowered mixed-genotype autopsy series (Yang 2023 PMID:37317638: 5 vs 4 ALS-TDP p=0.1 + 1 vs 2 ALS-SOD1, with higher cortical p62+ astrocytes and fewer spinal Iba1+ microglia) do not constitute published powered RCT futility; S02 (CHEMBL4297372; originated in SOD1/ferroptosis models by Barnham, Donnelly, Crouch & Southon et al. 2020 PMID:31655003) is retained on the low-priority Tier 3 watchlist behind 5 clinical, autopsy, PK ([MODEL_PRIOR] 53.2 nM = ~47x gap + Cu(I) transchelation), and mechanistic hurdles.
discriminating_next_test: Require public release and independent statistical audit of unblinded Phase 2/3 NCT04082832 ALSFRS-R/ECAS outcomes alongside 10-100 nM vs 2.5 uM intact unbound CuATSM concentration-response and radical-trapping ferroptosis target-engagement deconvolution in TDP-43-depleted human sALS iPSC-MNs before any renewed clinical consideration.

name: Mycophenolate mofetil
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Verified Bye 2025 2.5 uM paired rescue +1.2792d across 15 valid sALS lines (12/15 >0d, p=0.00293, q=0.02090, Rank #10/107; true IDs CHEMBL1456/CHEMBL866, fixing intake CHEMBL1230607 typo).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: At 1,000 mg PO BID transplant ceiling (NDA050722 CellCept: active MPA MW 320.34 is 97% albumin-bound, fu=0.03), human Cu,plasma,avg (~310-470 nM) sits 5.3-8.1x below 2.5 uM while >35x above lymphoid IMPDH2 Ki (~7-10 nM, PMID:7903306), and OAT3/MRP-effluxed anionic MPA (pKa 4.5) yields [MODEL_PRIOR] Cu,brain ~15-55 nM (45-165x below 2.5 uM neuronal screen); carries FDA Boxed Warnings (embryofetal toxicity, lymphoma/malignancies, serious infections) plus Section 5 PML/neutropenia warnings, and open-label Phase 2 ALS 4-drug immunosuppression trial NCT01884571 (Fournier et al. 2018 PMID:29308669: basiliximab + tacrolimus + MMF + prednisone, N=31) had 0/31 responders, no ALSFRS-R slowing vs pretreatment lead-in (p=0.200), and only 18/31 (58%) completing the treatment regimen (23/31 [74%] completing the study; 1 AE withdrawal, 2 deaths, 2 patient withdrawals, 3 disease-progression stops).
factual_justification: Active mycophenolic acid faces a 45-165-fold [MODEL_PRIOR] human unbound CNS deficit (~15-55 nM vs 2,500 nM screen; 97% albumin binding fu=0.03, NDA050722, Cu,plasma ~310-470 nM) bounded by peripheral IMPDH2 cytostasis (Ki ~7-10 nM, PMID:7903306), FDA Boxed Warnings (serious infections, lymphoma, teratogenicity) + Section 5 PML risk, and 0/31 responders (p=0.200 vs pretreatment lead-in; 18/31 regimen completers, 23/31 study completers) in 4-drug ALS trial NCT01884571 (PMID:29308669; scoped to pan-lymphocyte IMPDH ablation, preserving low-dose IL-2 Treg expansion).

name: Tamoxifen
causal_vs_reactive_assessment: UNTESTED_MICROMOLAR_CAD_PHOSPHOLIPIDOSIS_HYPOTHESIS: Plausible untested cationic-amphiphilic phospholipidosis/PKC regime at 2.5 uM vs ~3-15 nM [MODEL_PRIOR] unbound CNS PK
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Verified Bye 2025 2.5 uM paired rescue +1.2742d across 16 sALS lines (13/16 >0d, p=0.00316, q=0.02104, Rank #11/107).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Although total brain tamoxifen is 40-100x serum due to membrane/lysosomal lipid trapping (Lien et al. 1991 PMID:2021551, fu,brain <<0.0002; cLogP ~6.0-6.3, >99% bound), [MODEL_PRIOR] unbound aqueous brain exposure at 40-80 mg/d (~2.6 nM parent; ~3-15 nM combined with N-desmethyltamoxifen & P-gp-effluxed endoxifen) sits 165-800x below the 2.5 uM screen (where cationic-amphiphilic phospholipidosis/PKC modulation in low-protein media is a plausible untested hypothesis, Tummino et al. 2021 Science PMID:34326236); carries NDA021807 Boxed Warnings (stroke, pulmonary embolism, uterine malignancies), recorded 2 pulmonary embolisms and 3 DVTs (event-level counts across 38 tamoxifen-treated participants) plus 4/17 (23.5%) T80 deaths with untreated-rate ALSFRS-R decline in 38-wk placebo-less selection RCT NCT01257581 (Babu et al. 2020 PMID:31608711, N=60), and showed transient 3- and 6-mo differences attenuating to null at 12 mo in Chen et al. 2020 (PMID:32481440, NCT02166944, N=18) alongside conference-reported dose-comparison study NCT00214110 (N=100, unpublished in peer-reviewed full text).
factual_justification: Combined parent + active metabolite [MODEL_PRIOR] unbound human brain exposure (~3-15 nM at 40-80 mg/d; Lien et al. 1991 PMID:2021551 lipid trapping) is 165-800-fold below the 2.5 uM screen concentration (plausibly an untested cationic-amphiphilic phospholipidosis/PKC regime, Tummino et al. 2021 PMID:34326236), bounded by FDA Boxed Warnings (stroke, PE, uterine malignancy), thromboembolic events (2 PE and 3 DVT events across 38 tamoxifen recipients) in ALS selection RCT NCT01257581 (Babu et al. 2020 PMID:31608711, N=60), null 12-mo endpoint in Chen et al. 2020 (PMID:32481440, N=18), and unpublished NCT00214110 (N=100).

name: Lonafarnib / Tipifarnib (FTIs)
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Lonafarnib (CHEMBL298734, FTase IC50=1.9 nM) and Tipifarnib (CHEMBL289228, FTase IC50=0.57-0.90 nM) potently inhibit protein farnesyltransferase in biochemical assays and reduce mutant progerin/Rhes farnesylation in non-ALS models.
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Excluded on modeled CNS exposure, clinical tolerability, and predicted YKT6 prenylation antagonism (untested — not in 107-drug library — in Bye 2025 screen): (1) Predicted directional liability: although sub-stoichiometric FTIs improved synucleinopathy/tauopathy models via Rhes/closed-YKT6 modulation (Cuddy et al. 2019 PMID:31648898; Hernandez et al. 2019 PMID:30918111), human GGTase-III (PTAR1/RABGGTB, PDB 6J74 PMID:32128853; Sakata et al. 2021 PMID:33035318) biochemically requires prior FTase Cys195 farnesylation to geranylgeranylate YKT6 Cys194 for Golgi/lysosomal trafficking (pan-essential DepMap Chronos=-1.5425), predicting that FTIs would impair YKT6 diprenylation in TDP-43-depleted ALS neurons already carrying YKT6 APA (padj=4.57e-40) + PTAR1 170-bp Exon-2 frameshift skipping (chr9:69750781-69750950(-), mod_3=2, MOESM11 line 4145 group E(PSI) 0.156->0.369 [MAJIQ shrunk dPSI=+0.1563], source MAJIQ 'FDR' [p_d_psi_0.05]=3.256e-6; direct FTI testing in ALS neurons remains unperformed); (2) Unbound CNS PK deficit: Lonafarnib (NDA213969, MW 638.82, PPB>=99%) achieves Cmax,u<=42.2 nM at 150 mg/m2 BID and [MODEL_PRIOR] Cu,brain ~2.1-8.4 nM vs 70-500 nM cellular IC50 (Tipifarnib [MODEL_PRIOR] Cu,brain ~2-13 nM vs 2-75 nM sensitive-substrate IC50); (3) ALS-hostile human toxicity: Zokinvy Table 4 (N=63 pediatric Hutchinson-Gilford progeria patients at 150 mg/m2 BID) records 90% vomiting, 81% diarrhea, 37% weight loss (prognostically deleterious in ALS), 35% myelosuppression, +19 ms QTcF, and strong CYP3A autoinhibition, while Tipifarnib oncology regimens cause dose-limiting Grade 3/4 myelosuppression and neuropathy (Crul et al. 2002 PMID:12039935).
factual_justification: Excluded on [MODEL_PRIOR] human unbound CNS exposure limits (Lonafarnib Cu,brain ~2-8 nM vs 70-500 nM cellular IC50; Tipifarnib ~2-13 nM, NDA213969), ALS-hostile clinical toxicities (pediatric progeria Zokinvy label: 37% weight loss, 81-90% GI toxicity, 35% myelosuppression, +19 ms QTcF; oncology Tipifarnib myelosuppression/neuropathy DLT PMID:12039935; untested in Bye 2025 screen), and predicted biochemical antagonism of sequential FTase Cys195 -> GGTase-III Cys194 dual prenylation on YKT6 (PDB 6J74 PMID:32128853; untested directly in ALS neurons) atop TDP-43 PTAR1 170-bp Exon-2 skipping (despite mouse tauopathy FTI rescue PMID:30918111; preserving pro-prenylation YKT6/PTAR1 rescue in C023).

name: SARM1 (Axonal NADase)
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Rare constitutively active ARM-domain GoF variants enrich in human ALS (Gilley 2021 PMID:34796871; Bloom 2022 PMID:34991663; near-full-length autoinhibited 7ANW/7DJT octamer inter-protomer ARM-TIR latch 3.07-5.47A vs 37.8-65.4A intra-chain, cumulative validated GoF AF=0.000378 [~0.076% carriers] vs benign P332Q AF=0.986%, 97 hom; 0/12 single-gene SARM1 ClinVar P/LP [6 opposite-strand SLC46A1 records]), executing Wallerian NAD+ catastrophe; elevated protein in small-sample C9FTD iPSC neurons (+0.675, p=0.0268, n=3 vs 3); no population depletion of heterozygous pLoF variants in Open Targets / legacy constraint (obs/exp=60/65.1, LOEUF=1.143) or gnomAD v4.1 MANE (obs/exp=60/52.6, LOEUF=1.413; distinct from biallelic KO phenotyping).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Postmortem end-stage bulk RNA is lower (-0.307) due to projection-neuron dropout, clinical SARM1 space now spans three Ph1/2 programs — Disarm-lineage orthosteric base-exchange prodrug Lilly LY3873862 (NCT07883590 [Ph1 Not Yet Recruiting], PMID:33406435), oral reversible orthosteric inhibitor Nura/TRICALS NB-4746 (NCT07369076, undisclosed structure), and Sironax oral allosteric inhibitor SIR2501 (CTR20253552 China ALS Ph1b/2a, NCT07765446 US paclitaxel CIPN Ph2 n=18, ANZCTR 387449 HV SAD/MAD N=82 up to 600 mg/150 mg QD, ASCO 2026 10.1200/JCO.2026.44.16_suppl.12148, SfN 2026 PSTR091 15 Nov 2026 unreviewed congress poster; WO2024125624A1/WO2024222835A1/WO2026086928A1) plus preclinical ASHA-624 — 2026 Commun Chem (PMID:42156967, PDB 9TZY) warns orthosteric BEXi scaffolds risk paradoxical sub-inhibitory SARM1 activation (0.05x-0.30x Kd), undisclosed SIR2501 structure leaves unresolved chronic thiol-reactive Cys311 ARM covalency (PDB 7DJT class, PMID:33944777) vs reversible non-covalent ARM/ARM-TIR T-lock (ASHA-624 class), and healthy-volunteer circulating plasma cADPR (ASCO #12148) is >90-95% ecto-CD38/BST1-generated (PMID:32087251; PMID:16750163) while CIPN DRGs lie outside the BBB.
factual_justification: Core Track B target backed by human ALS rare GoF genetics, TDP-43Q331K & TBI-accelerated Sarm1-/- axonal/NMJ rescue (White et al. 2019 PMID:31661035 [noting unimproved rotarod latency]; PMID:39791335; whereas uninjured mSOD1G93A Sarm1KO lowered Simoa serum NfL & GFAP and protected sciatic axons/VGluT2+ synapses without rescuing MN somata or survival in Collins et al. 2022 PMID:35863521 — motivating our project's prospective trial-design choices of non-SOD1 enrollment and MScanFit MUNE/CMAP + CSF NPTX2 monitoring alongside blood NfL), parallel axonal protection alongside STMN2 (Krus et al. 2022 PMID:35767949), elevated C9-FTD iPSC neuronal protein (+0.675, p=0.0268, n=6, PMID:42789089), and low heterozygous pLoF constraint (Open Targets LOEUF=1.143; gnomAD v4.1 MANE LOEUF=1.413); across 4 clinical-stage SARM1 inhibitors from 3 sponsors (LY3873862 NCT07883590 [ALS Ph1 Not Yet Recruiting; HV NCT05492201 N=84 completed], NB-4746 NCT07369076, Phase 1 HV covalent allosteric NB-9402 ACTRN12626000650392/WO2025090514A1, and SIR2501 CTR20253552/NCT07765446/WO2026086928A1; originating isoquinoline base-exchange scaffolds in Bosanac et al. 2021 PMID:33964142) and preclinical ASHA-624 / covalent Cys311 EV-99 (PMID:35994671), proposed CNS-penetrant non-covalent inter-protomer ARM-TIR T-locks (PDB 7ANW/7DJT, 3.2-3.3A Glu252-Gln585 interface proximity; Cys311Ala selectivity gated prospectively) are designed to avoid biphasic base-exchange activation (compound-specific washout behavior remains untested).
discriminating_next_test: Prioritize CNS-penetrant reversible non-covalent inter-protomer ARM-TIR T-lock glues (ASHA-624 class; verifying Cys311-independent binding via Cys311Ala SARM1 vs covalent Cys311 PDB 7DJT benchmark and benchmarking undisclosed allosteric SIR2501 [CTR20253552 ALS Ph1b/2a, NCT07765446 CIPN Ph2, SfN 2026 PSTR091]) head-to-head against Disarm-lineage 3-chain TIR-gluing base-exchange inhibitor (BEXi) prodrugs (PDB 9TZY, LY3873862 NCT07883590, PMID:33406435, PMID:42156967) and empirically decoupled reversible orthosteric NB-4746 (NCT07369076) across full trough-to-peak and 48-72 h simulated oral CNS washout curves (5x -> 0.03x IC50, modeling missed doses in bulbar dysphagia) in microfluidic WT, Cys311Ala, and isogenic SARM1 p.L223P ARM-GoF negative-control human sALS motor axons +/- STMN2 splice rescue (bracketing the 1.00x parallel microtubule-remodeling Bliss survival lower bound per 10.64898/2026.11.07.764673 [PREPRINT] & PMID:35767949 against the ~2-7x [med ~3x, MODEL_PRIOR] NMNAT2-epistatic MWC upper bound), paired with enzymatic ecto-CD38/BST1 counter-screening (since >90-95% CD38-derived basal fluid cADPR caps 90% selective SARM1 blockade at ~5-10% drop so a -50% cell-free plasma drop implies ~45-50% CD38 inhibition [MODEL_PRIOR], PMID:32087251/PMID:16750163, while CIPN DRGs lie outside the BBB) and anchoring human Phase 1b PD on unbound CSF Ctrough,u >= IC80 (Kp,uu >= 0.30), zero washout CSF pNfH/plasma NfL spike, and exploratory L1CAM/ATP1A3+ neuron-derived EV cADPR:NAD+ while reserving SARM1 KD ASO (PMID:40473123; given ~30-40% residual NADase ceiling [MODEL_PRIOR] at 100x Kd in Binomial hetero-octamer d_lock=6.5 GoF heterozygotes) for <1% ARM-broken GoF carriers.

name: Low-Dose Aldesleukin (IL-2) in Low-pNfH Stratum
evidence_proves_hypothesis: In MIROCALS Phase 2b (NCT03039673, PMID:40354799, Lancet May 2025, N=220 randomized of 304 screened, 90 deaths; primary unadjusted ITT HR=0.81, 95% CI 0.54-1.22, p=0.33; CHEMBL1201438), SAP-prespecified covariate-adjusted Cox + continuous CSF pNfH x Treatment modeling was positive (conditional adj HR=0.32 at reference pNfH=0, 95% CI 0.14-0.73, p=0.0070; interaction HR=1.0003/pg/mL, p=0.0011; secondary ALSFRS-R slope interaction F=3.95, p=0.048), with 48% 21-mo mortality hazard reduction in the 750-3,700 pg/mL BioVendor ELISA stratum (partitioned via baseline CSF pNfH visual distribution assessment in mmc1.pdf pp. 13, 23 alongside survival cutoff comparisons across pNfH thresholds in WO2024121173A1; cf. WO2021176044A1, temporal order/independence unresolved; n=154, 57 deaths, HR=0.52, 95% CI 0.30-0.89, p=0.016; <750 pg/mL LLOQ n=19 had 0 deaths; pooled <=3,700 pg/mL n=173/220 randomized [78.6% LP; 173/304 = 56.9% of all 304 screened, i.e., screened participants randomized with baseline CSF pNfH <=3,700 pg/mL] HR=0.57, 95% CI 0.33-0.97, p=0.037) alongside sustained Day-112 trough FOXP3+ Treg expansion (p<0.0001) and plasma CCL2 reduction (p<0.05 at Day-112 trough, p<0.0001 at Days 8 & 120; CSF CCL2/pNfH NS at Day 112); Al Khleifat et al. 2026 (PMID:42836993, PMC13642438, J Neurol 273:643) showed inside MIROCALS (N=220) that clinical TRICALS risk shares only r^2=12.7% (r=0.357) of variance with CSF pNfH and contributes less treatment-interaction information (nested dChi2=4.76, LRT p=0.029 / Wald p=0.025 vs dChi2=14.24 for pNfH x treatment; adding pNfH to TRICALS dChi2=44.39; combined model reference HR=0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.63, p=0.002).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Primary unadjusted ITT log-rank test missed significance (HR=0.81, 95% CI 0.54-1.22, p=0.33; >3,700 pg/mL n=47 [33/90 deaths] showed no demonstrated benefit HR=1.37, 95% CI 0.68-2.75, p=0.38, and 3,700 pg/mL was described via baseline visual assessment in mmc1.pdf alongside survival cutoff comparisons in WO2024121173A1 rather than externally pre-locked), IL2/IL2RA has 0 human ALS genetics, EMA/MHRA/UK MND CSG declined approval pending Phase 3 proof (note MIROCALS low-dose IL-2 + neurofilament/CCL2 IP under AP-HP/Sorbonne/MIROCALS-consortium patents WO2021176044A1 & WO2024121173A1 is exclusively licensed to ILTOO Pharma ILT-101), commercial pNfH immunoassays exhibit ~1.8x-4.5x inter-platform pg/mL calibrator offsets (PMID:31251725; PMID:29054919; cf. BioVendor ELISA in PMID:40354799 vs MSD ECLIA cited in PMID:42836993), Phase 2/3 ALSTARS (NCT07161999, ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, N=137 enrolled across 3 baseline serum NfL tiers on 24-wk ALSFRS-R; US12312389B2) tests dual-biologic COYA 302 (1 MIU rhIL-2 + 125 mg CTLA4-Ig q14d vs q28d; <0.5% BBB entry, CD28 blockade PMID:30683697/PMID:36920087 vs IL-2 STAT5 rescue PMID:42086904) without baseline CSF pNfH exclusion or a single-agent IL-2 arm alongside cellular Treg trials (RAPA-501 NCT04220190, CK0803 REGALS NCT05695521, completed Treg+IL-2 NCT04055623, and null rapamycin RAP-ALS NCT03359538), ALS FOXP3+ Tregs risk TSDR methylation drift + NK/eosinophil/sCD25 sinks, and zero prospective Phase 3 trials gated on calibrated CSF pNfH <=3,700 pg/mL have completed.

name: Ultrahigh-Dose Methylcobalamin (Rozebalamin)
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Phase 3 JETALS RCT (NCT03548311, Oki et al. 2022 JAMA Neurol PMID:35532908, N=130 randomized / N=129 FAS [65 vs 64] / 126 Wk-16 completers, <=12m from symptom onset, 50 mg IM 2x/wk; CHEMBL4297672) slowed 16-wk MMRM ALSFRS-R decline by 43% (+1.97 pts, -2.66 vs -4.63, 95% CI 0.44-3.50, exact p=0.012; +2.11 pts [p=0.01] in n=116 concomitant riluzole) and lowered plasma homocysteine (-37.2%, p<0.001), confirming Kaji et al. 2019's <=12m stratum (PMID:30636701, n=144 HR=0.498, p<0.025) and earning Japan MHLW approval on Sept 24, 2024 (Rozebalamin 25 mg x2 vials = 50 mg IM twice weekly).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Prior broad-window (<=3 yr onset) Phase 2/3 RCT missed overall co-primaries (Kaji et al. 2019 PMID:30636701, NCT00444613, N=373 randomized / N=370 FAS: 50 mg survival p=0.087, ALSFRS-R p=0.19), 16-wk JETALS secondary FVC (p=0.39) was non-significant and Rozebalamin remains unapproved by FDA/EMA (0 active US/EU Phase 3 trials), and unshielded 2.5 uM methylcobalamin (~2.1-2.3x human 50 mg IM plasma Cmax ~1.1-1.2 uM) scored -3.60d (q=0.00246, Rank #105/107) in Bye 2025, plausibly via ~450-488 nm live-imaging Co-C bond photolysis into aquo/hydroxocobalamin + methyl/ROS radicals.
factual_justification: Reclassified as a regionally approved Standard-of-Care (SOC) clinical benchmark (Japan MHLW Sept 24, 2024 Rozebalamin 50 mg IM twice weekly for ALS functional slowing, anchored in JETALS <=12m onset N=129 FAS +1.97 ALSFRS-R pts, p=0.012, PMID:35532908) and iPSC-screen Co-C photolability calibration benchmark.
discriminating_next_test: Account for concomitant 50 mg IM mecobalamin use when stratifying Japanese ALS trial cohorts (<=12m onset; noting Rozebalamin efficacy is not yet confirmed outside Japan or in non-Japanese East-Asian cohorts), and pair dark-shielded vs ~450-488 nm blue-light-irradiated + hydroxocobalamin controls in live-imaging iPSC-MN screens.

name: Censavudine (TPN-101) in ALS-TE Subtype
evidence_proves_hypothesis: Phase 2a NCT04993755 (mixed N=42 C9orf72-ALS + FTD safety cohort, 400 mg/d PO TPN-101 / CHEMBL124363; alongside completed PSP Ph2a NCT04993768 N=42, AGS Ph2 ISG program, and ROME Therapeutics non-nucleoside LINE-1 RT discovery context) reported favorable safety, reduced CSF IL-6 & NfL, ~50% slower 24-wk vital capacity decline in the C9-ALS subgroup (-8.4% vs -16.5% placebo; while 24-wk randomized ALSFRS-R change was -7.2 vs -6.7), and May 2025 selection of TPN-101 for the Phase 2/3 HEALEY ALS Platform Trial (Master Protocol NCT04297683); within motor ALS cortex, ALS-TE elevates IFNAR2 both vs ALS-Ox (+0.2793, p=6.32e-8, GC+cellcomp adj_p=3.87e-9, AUC=0.7698) and vs Control (+0.1920, p=6.62e-4, adj_p=0.0376) while retaining intact TYK2 (+0.5763 vs Ox, p=5.52e-9) and STAT2 (+0.3103 vs Ox, p=5.14e-8).
evidence_disproves_hypothesis: Primary re-analysis of O'Neill 2025 (DS001_ONEILL) shows cortical ALS-TE prevalence is 13.40% (41/306 all cortical motor-ALS donors; 13.53% = 41/303 excluding 3 multi-region discordant donors; 11.52% [22/191] in C9-neg ALS+ALS/FTD and 11.60% [21/181] in C9-neg ALS), spinal cord ALS-TE prevalence was not estimable because O'Neill's separate two-class spinal classifier (N=331) assigned only Glia-cord or Ox-cord, and postmortem cortical ALS-TE TYK2 (-0.0732, p=0.465) & STAT2 (+0.0153, p=0.798) plus bulk ISGs (ISG15/IFIT1/MX1/OAS1/IRF9) are flat vs Control, while NCT04993755 remains unpublished in peer-reviewed form (randomized 24-wk ALSFRS-R -7.2 vs -6.7), no validated living-CSF ALS-TE enrichment assay exists for HEALEY Ph2/3 sporadic enrollment (published ORF1p Simoa PMID:40050409 was developed for ovarian-cancer serum rather than ALS CSF), nucleoside prodrug TPN-101 inhibits LINE-1 ORF2p reverse transcriptase (cDNA -> cGAS-STING) rather than Pol II inverted-repeat dsRNA duplexes (cdsRNA -> MDA5/RIG-I -> IFNAR1/TYK2, Konig et al. 2026 PMID:41832177) and requires unmeasured post-mitotic human MN vs glial TPN-101-TP triphosphorylation, deucravacitinib is P-gp/BCRP-excluded across the BBB, and brain-penetrant BHV-8000 (TLL-041, early PD NCT06976268; sponsor PK disclosure Kp,uu=0.539, 20 mg QD Cu,brain,avg ~172 nM) is an orthosteric dual TYK2/JAK1 JH1 inhibitor that co-blocks gp130/JAK1-STAT3.
factual_justification: Oral LINE-1 RT inhibitor TPN-101 (TRL_5; selected May 2025 for Phase 2/3 HEALEY ALS Platform Trial following mixed N=42 C9orf72-ALS/FTD Phase 2a NCT04993755 & PSP NCT04993768) showed encouraging C9-ALS subgroup biomarker (CSF IL-6/NfL) and vital-capacity signals (-8.4% vs -16.5%, with randomized ALSFRS-R -7.2 vs -6.7), and cortical ALS-TE elevates IFNAR2 above Control, yet efficacy in sporadic ALS-TE remains unproven pending peer-reviewed NCT04993755 publication, living-CSF ORF1p/L1HS validation for the ~13.4-13.5% cortical ALS-TE subgroup (spinal ALS-TE prevalence not estimable under O'Neill's 2-class cord classifier, N=331), epistasis deconvolution of ORF2p cDNA vs Pol II cdsRNA->TYK2 signaling (PMID:41832177), and post-mitotic human MN vs glial TPN-101-TP triphosphorylation verification.
discriminating_next_test: Anchor Phase 2/3 HEALEY ALS Platform Trial sporadic biomarker stratification by disaggregating three biological layers alongside peer-reviewed NCT04993755 C9-ALS vs FTD publication and human iPSC-MN vs microglial TPN-101-TP LC-MS/MS phosphorylation verification: (1) cryptic HDGFL2 (PMID:38278991/PMID:42854693) solely as the upstream pan-TDP-43 pathology gate, (2) direct retroelement cargo (adapting ovarian-cancer serum LINE-1 ORF1p Simoa PMID:40050409 to ALS CSF/plasma + CSF EV L1HS RNA/cDNA) as the subtype-specific ALS-TE enrichment gate calibrated to 13.40% (41/306; 13.53% = 41/303 non-discordant; 11.52% [22/191] C9-neg ALS+ALS/FTD; 11.60% [21/181] C9-neg ALS) cortical prevalence, and (3) ultrasensitive CSF IL-6/CXCL10 + cGAS-STING vs cdsRNA->IFNAR1/TYK2 epistasis (testing TPN-101 vs brain-penetrant dual TYK2/JAK1 JH1 BHV-8000 [sponsor PK Kp,uu=0.539] and BBB-penetrant allosteric TYK2-JH2 probes, given deucravacitinib P-gp efflux, PMID:41832177).
